ev.q: 2021 data indicate an increase in suicide to 48,183, nearly returning to the 2018 peak (48,344)
Suicide rates among persons aged 10–24 years increased significantly during 2018–2021 among Black persons
Annual number of suicides and rates of suicide* (suicides per 100,000 population)
Age-adjusted 2021 suicide rates were highest among non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native (AI/AN) persons (28.1 per 100,000) overall
Among those aged 25–44 years, rates increased significantly overall (5%) and among AI/AN (33.7%)
Age-adjusted rates (suicides per 100,000 population) were calculated using the direct method and the 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
Suicides were identified from the National Vital Statistics System multiple cause-of-death mortality files for 2018–2021.
Differences in rates from 2018 to 2021 were compared using z-tests when deaths were ≥100

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted rates and 95% CIs were calculated using the direct method and the 2000 U.S. standard population.
Differences in rates from 2018 to 2021 were compared using z-tests when deaths were ≥100
When deaths were <100, differences in rates were considered significant if CIs based on a gamma distribution did not overlap.
Z-tests were used if the number of deaths was ≥100; nonoverlapping CIs based on the gamma method were used if the number of deaths was ≤100).
